hard_deny: Creating git commits, merges, rebases or cherry-picks on any branch whose name contains 'release'.
Pushing or merging anything into a branch whose name contains 'release'.
Creating merge requests or pull requests (gh pr create, glab mr create, API calls, push options).
Editing operating-system functions or settings: registry, services, scheduled tasks, firewall, users, execution policy, system directories.
Deleting or modifying any data on remote resources or network drives (UNC paths, mapped network drives, SSH/SFTP/SCP targets, cloud storage, remote repositories).
soft_deny: Any git push, even to non-release branches, without the user's explicit confirmation in this conversation.
Installing applications or packages, or downloading and running scripts from the internet, without explicit user confirmation.
Reading or printing passwords, keys, tokens, credentials or other security secrets without explicit user confirmation.
Sending any data to the internet (HTTP requests, uploads, web searches, publishing, external MCP services) without explicit user confirmation.
